outputText: We need answer user: "Explain why local inference benchmarks should report prompt prefill throughput, decode throughput, and time to first token." Need provide explanation. Need final answer. Need likely discuss LLM inference phases: prefill/prompt processing vs decode token generation. Local benchmarks need these metrics because they capture different bottlenecks: prefill throughput (tokens/s for prompt) measures how fast model can process input context, KV cache build, attention over prompt, batched prompt, memory bandwidth/compute, affects latency for long contexts and RAG. Decode throughput (tokens/s generated) measures autoregressive generation speed, often memory-bandwidth bound, affects sustained output speed, batch size, quantization, KV cache. Time to first token (TTFT) measures user-perceived latency from request to first generated token, includes prompt prefill, scheduling, loading, overhead; important for interactive use. Reporting all three avoids misleading single throughput number: high prefill throughput doesn't imply fast generation; high decode throughput doesn't imply low initial latency; TTFT can be dominated by prefill for long prompts, while decode throughput dominates long outputs. Also local inference specifics: hardware constraints, batch size, context length, quantization, CPU/GPU, memory, thermal, OS overhead.
